forces: Orchestra, organ and piano four hands
performers: Philharmonic-Symphony Orchestra of New York; Charles Munch; Édouard Nies-Berger, organ
intro: Saint-Saëns joined two movements into each half of his symphony, and the organ first enters in the Poco adagio. Charles Munch and the New York Philharmonic-Symphony made the work’s second recording in 1947.

B · Poco adagio: organ under strings

cues.title: Adagio introduction, woodwinds
cues.text: The Adagio opens with broken phrases for oboe, cor anglais and bassoon. Hugh Macdonald described these phrases as plaintive and heard in them a tone poem by Liszt.
cues.evidence: Hugh Macdonald’s programme note on the Symphony No. 3, Boston Symphony Orchestra. https://www.bso.org/works/saint-saens-symphony-no-3-organ-symphony The note calls the introduction’s phrases broken and plaintive, from oboe, English horn and bassoon.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Allegro, string figure
cues.text: The Allegro begins immediately. A restless figure in the strings becomes a theme, and it returns in many guises later in the symphony.
cues.evidence: Hugh Macdonald’s programme note on the Symphony No. 3, Boston Symphony Orchestra. https://www.bso.org/works/saint-saens-symphony-no-3-organ-symphony The note says the Allegro arrives immediately and that the strings’ restless accompanying figure recurs in many guises.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: First performance, London, 19 May 1886
cues.text: Saint-Saëns conducted the first performance at St James’s Hall, London, for the Royal Philharmonic Society, which had commissioned it. In the first half he played a Beethoven concerto, with Arthur Sullivan conducting.
cues.evidence: Hugh Macdonald’s programme note on the Symphony No. 3, Boston Symphony Orchestra. https://www.bso.org/works/saint-saens-symphony-no-3-organ-symphony The Société Camille Saint-Saëns chronology gives the date and place. https://camille-saint-saens.org/1882-1888/

cues.title: Munch’s Columbia recording, 1947
cues.text: Munch’s Columbia set was the work’s second recording, after Piero Coppola’s French HMV version of 1930, and Munch’s first in the United States. It was made at Carnegie Hall on 10 November 1947.
cues.evidence: The Internet Archive item for Columbia Masterworks set MM-747, with the transferor’s side-by-side description. https://archive.org/details/mm-747-saint-saens-sym-3-i Pristine Audio’s note for PASC448 also calls it Munch’s first American recording. https://www.pristineclassical.com/products/pasc448

cues.title: First organ entry, slow movement
cues.text: The organ plays for the first time at the start of the slow movement. It holds soft chords in D♭ major beneath a theme in the strings.
cues.evidence: The Internet Archive item for Columbia Masterworks set MM-747, with the transferor’s side-by-side description. https://archive.org/details/mm-747-saint-saens-sym-3-i The transferor puts the start of the Adagio part at 8:47 in this file, and the organ plays on sides 3 and 4. Hugh Macdonald’s programme note on the Symphony No. 3, Boston Symphony Orchestra. https://www.bso.org/works/saint-saens-symphony-no-3-organ-symphony

cues.title: Second statement of the string melody
cues.text: The string melody returns, now played by clarinet, two horns and two trombones across three octaves. Pizzicato double basses recall an earlier theme before the main tune returns.
cues.evidence: Hugh Macdonald’s programme note on the Symphony No. 3, Boston Symphony Orchestra. https://www.bso.org/works/saint-saens-symphony-no-3-organ-symphony The note describes this second statement and the pizzicato basses.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Return of the main tune
cues.text: The main tune returns, and the movement closes. Hugh Macdonald, in his programme note for the Boston Symphony Orchestra, called the close serene.
cues.evidence: Hugh Macdonald’s programme note on the Symphony No. 3, Boston Symphony Orchestra. https://www.bso.org/works/saint-saens-symphony-no-3-organ-symphony The note describes the reprise of the main tune and the serene close.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

composer.epithet: Pianist from the age of ten and organist for twenty years, known for the Organ Symphony, a dance of skeletons featuring xylophone, and a zoo suite he forbade anyone to publish.
facts: Piano with Stamaty; organ with François Benoist and composition under Halévy at the Paris Conservatoire, from 1848
Organist of La Madeleine, 1857–77; piano professor at the École Niedermeyer, 1861–65; co-founder of the Société nationale de musique, 1871
Symphonies, ten concertos, four symphonic poems, operas, organ music, songs and chamber music; also plays, poems and articles
Spent most winters from 1873 in Algeria, Egypt or the Canary Islands, and kept no fixed address from 1889 to 1905

quote.text: I have given it all that I had to give. What I have done I shall never do again.
quote.source: Saint-Saëns on the Organ Symphony, as quoted in Hugh Macdonald’s Boston Symphony Orchestra note

composer.background:
Camille Saint-Saëns was born at 3 rue du Jardinet in Paris on 9 October 1835. His father, a clerk in the Ministry of the Interior, died of consumption on 30 December, when the boy was not yet three months old. He was a sickly child and was raised by two widows, his mother Clémence and her aunt Charlotte Masson, who taught him piano. At two and a half he pressed the keys one at a time and waited for each note to die away before playing the next. By his own account he already listened at that age to the kettle on the drawing-room fire, which he called a “microscopic oboe”, and to its sound swelling until the water boiled.

Children’s pieces gave the left hand nothing to do. “The bass doesn’t sing,” he told his teachers in disgust, and was given Haydn and Mozart. On 6 May 1846, aged ten, he played Beethoven’s Third Piano Concerto and a Mozart concerto in B♭ at the Salle Pleyel, and played the whole programme from memory. Someone asked his mother what he would play when he was twenty. “He will play his own,” she said.
